parts.name: green body shell

physics.Basic_description: The main red-painted metal structure comprising the fuel tank base and the top chimney cap with a matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the fuel reservoir at the bottom and protects the flame/vents air at the top.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can firmly grasp the cylindrical base or the upper chimney section to lift or stabilize the lantern.
physics.reason: Standard sheet metal construction for lanterns; the base is a thin-walled tank and the top is a stamped shell.

parts.description: The main red-painted metal structure comprising the fuel tank base and the top chimney cap with a matte finish.

parts.name: globe glass

physics.Basic_description: A translucent, pale green cylindrical glass enclosure situated in the center of the lantern.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the flame from wind while allowing light to escape and containing heat.
physics.Grasped_description: Fragile and smooth; a gripper should avoid grasping this directly to prevent breakage or slippage.
physics.reason: Glass globes are blown or molded thin shells enclosing the combustion chamber.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
